From 8c88181ed452707f3815827225517b1964463b95 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jesper Dangaard Brouer <brouer@redhat.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Feb 2018 12:48:12 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] bpf: Sync kernel ABI header with tooling header for
 bpf_common.h

I recently fixed up a lot of commits that forgot to keep the tooling
headers in sync.  And then I forgot to do the same thing in commit
cb5f7334d479 ("bpf: add comments to BPF ld/ldx sizes"). Let correct
that before people notice ;-).

Lawrence did partly fix/sync this for bpf.h in commit d6d4f60c3a09
("bpf: add selftest for tcpbpf").

Fixes: cb5f7334d479 ("bpf: add comments to BPF ld/ldx sizes")
Signed-off-by: Jesper Dangaard Brouer <brouer@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Daniel Borkmann <daniel@iogearbox.net>

diff --git a/tools/include/uapi/linux/bpf_common.h b/tools/include/uapi/linux/bpf_common.h
index 18be90725ab0..ee97668bdadb 100644
--- a/tools/include/uapi/linux/bpf_common.h
+++ b/tools/include/uapi/linux/bpf_common.h
@@ -15,9 +15,10 @@
 
 /* ld/ldx fields */
 #define BPF_SIZE(code)  ((code) & 0x18)
-#define		BPF_W		0x00
-#define		BPF_H		0x08
-#define		BPF_B		0x10
+#define		BPF_W		0x00 /* 32-bit */
+#define		BPF_H		0x08 /* 16-bit */
+#define		BPF_B		0x10 /*  8-bit */
+/* eBPF		BPF_DW		0x18    64-bit */
 #define BPF_MODE(code)  ((code) & 0xe0)
 #define		BPF_IMM		0x00
 #define		BPF_ABS		0x20
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `tools/include/uapi/linux/bpf_common.h`**
   - Added comments to the definitions of `BPF_W`, `BPF_H`, and `BPF_B` to clarify their corresponding bit sizes (32-bit, 16-bit, and 8-bit respectively).
   - Added a comment for `BPF_DW` indicating it represents a 64-bit value, although the actual definition for `BPF_DW` is not included in this patch.

### Relationships
The modifications in `bpf_common.h` are intended to synchronize the kernel ABI header with the tooling header, ensuring that the comments accurately reflect the intended use and size of the BPF (Berkeley Packet Filter) constants. This patch addresses an oversight from a previous commit (cb5f7334d479) that added comments to BPF ld/ldx sizes but did not update the tooling header accordingly. The changes help maintain consistency and clarity in the codebase, which is crucial for developers working with BPF.

Here is the root cause:

This oversight led to a lack of clarity regarding the bit sizes associated with the BPF constants, which could cause confusion for developers and potentially lead to incorrect usage of these constants in the code.

+#define		BPF_H		0x08 /* 16-bit */
+#define		BPF_B		0x10 /*  8-bit */

 #define BPF_MODE(code)  ((code) & 0xe0)

These definitions for BPF constants (BPF_W, BPF_H, BPF_B) were not accompanied by comments indicating their respective bit sizes, leading to confusion about their usage. This oversight occurred after a previous commit that added comments to BPF ld/ldx sizes, resulting in a lack of clarity in the tooling header (`bpf_common.h`).

```c
#define		BPF_W		0x00 /* 32-bit */
#define		BPF_H		0x08 /* 16-bit */
#define		BPF_B		0x10 /*  8-bit */
```
Reason:
The added comments next to each BPF constant provide clear documentation of the bit sizes associated with each constant (32-bit for BPF_W, 16-bit for BPF_H, and 8-bit for BPF_B). This synchronization with the kernel ABI header enhances clarity and prevents potential misuse of these constants by developers.
